land.text: the realm of Go-Daigo's restored imperial government, which Takauji overthrew ('Ashikaga Takauji was appointed Shōgun after overthrowing the Kenmu Restoration')

capitals.name: Heian-kyō (Kyoto)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Heian-kyō'. The Muromachi district of Kyoto gave the period its other name; Yoshiaki was driven out in 1573.

rulers.name: Ashikaga Yoshimitsu
rulers.note: Under him the Northern and Southern courts were combined in 1392.

rulers.name: Ashikaga Yoshinori
rulers.note: The bakufu's authority 'almost vanished by 1441 at the death of Ashikaga Yoshinori'.

rulers.name: Ashikaga Yoshiaki
rulers.note: Expelled from Kyoto by Oda Nobunaga in 1573.

correction.text: the Kenmu outline (Honshu, Shikoku and Kyushu) carried over as the realm the Ashikaga government claimed, in the years before Cliopatria starts its Ashikaga row

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives 'Established: 11 August 1336' and 'Takauji established his own military government in Kyoto', so the Ashikaga cannot wait for Cliopatria's 1344 row; Cliopatria shows the Kenmu label on this outline until 1343. The page gives no extent for the first years, and the Southern Court held ground (Yoshino from January 1337, Kyushu): see the contest events. The infobox gives no area, so no area check is possible.

320,516 km2, Honshu to Kyushu with Shikoku, identical to the Kamakura and Kenmu outlines; the infobox gives no area, so no ratio. This is the claimed national realm: the Southern Court contested Kyushu to 1385 and Yoshino to 1392 (contest events), and the Kantō was ruled from Kamakura (Kamakura-fu / Kantō kubō), which the page does not mention and the page budget did not reach: unverified. Cliopatria keeps the outline to 1458 although the page says the bakufu's authority 'almost vanished by 1441'.

322,236 km2: the 1344 outline plus about 1,700 km2 on the southern Oshima Peninsula of Hokkaido (bbox north to 41.98 N), the 'Twelve Garrisons of Dōnan' the Wajin held after Koshamain's revolt (1457-58). The page does not say the shogunate itself claimed them: Takeda Nobuhiro served Kakizaki Sueshige, lord of Hanazawa. Kept as Cliopatria draws it; the ledger gain is confidence 1.

979 km2 around Kyoto and southern Ōmi (bbox 135.76-136.13 E, 34.94-35.39 N). The page: in the Ōnin War (1467-1477) the shogunate 'became reduced to little more than a local political force in Kyoto'. Matches. The Yamashiro ikki set up a provisional government in Yamashiro in 1485-86 (Ōnin War page) but the Cliopatria shape is not changed for it.

879 km2, 100 km2 smaller than 1468-1539. No page opened dates the change; the Sengoku page has Miyoshi Nagayoshi defeating the 12th shogun Yoshiharu in 1547 and 'established control over the Kyoto area in 1549'. The gazetteer resolves the 1540 shape to the same grid cells as 1468-1539 (a cell is about 253 km2), so no ledger event is needed; kept.

1,055 km2, 176 km2 larger than 1540-1563. Page silent on the 1564 change (the Ashikaga page has Yoshiteru assassinated in 1565). The gazetteer resolves the 1564 shape to the same grid cells as 1540-1563, so no ledger event is needed; kept.

correction.text: the 1564-1571 Kyoto holding, held to the shogunate's abolition on 2 September 1573

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria's Ashikaga row ends in 1571 but the infobox gives 'Ashikaga shogunate abolished: 2 September 1573'; Yoshiaki, installed in Kyoto by Nobunaga in 1568, was not driven out until 1573.

region.text: Kyushu, where Takauji retreated in 1336 and imperial resistance lasted to the end of the period

ledger.note: 1336: the war for Kyushu begins. the page has Takauji allying with local Kyushu clans after retreating there in 1336, and imperial resistance in Kyushu lasting until the end of the period; it does not date the first Southern Court campaign in Kyushu, so 1336 is the retreat.

region.text: Kyoto, where Takauji established his government

ledger.note: 1336: Ashikaga Takauji sets up his military government in Kyoto. Infobox 'Established: 11 August 1336'; 'In 1336, Takauji established his own military government in Kyoto' (the infobox dates his shogunal reign from 1338). Takauji had entered the capital on 25 February 1336 and the Kenmu Restoration ended (Kenmu Restoration page); the Northern Court's Kōmyō was enthroned in September 1336.

region.text: the realm of the overthrown Kenmu Restoration

ledger.note: 1336: the shogunate takes over the Kenmu court's realm on paper. The page gives no extent; the realm is Cliopatria's Kenmu outline (Honshu, Shikoku, Kyushu), which Cliopatria carries to 1343 before its Ashikaga row begins in 1344. Real control was partial (see the Southern Court contests).

region.text: the mountains of Yoshino, where Go-Daigo set up his court

ledger.note: 1337: Go-Daigo sets up the Southern Court at Yoshino. 'Go-Daigo escaped from the capital in January 1337' and set up his court in the mountains of Yoshino; the period of the two courts lasts 'between 1336 and 1392'.

region.text: Kyushu, the last bastion of Southern Court resistance

ledger.note: 1385: the last Kyushu holdout submits. 'imperialist resistance collapsed with the defeat of the Kikuchi clan in 1381'; the last Kyushu domain submitted in 1385, after the campaign of Imagawa Sadayo (Ryōshun), appointed in 1370.

1392: the Southern Court yields and the two courts are one. 'On November 19, 1392, Emperor Go-Kameyama renounced the Japanese Imperial Treasures to the Northern Court', in exchange for an agreement to alternate the succession (which the Northern line broke in 1412).

region.text: the Twelve Garrisons of Dōnan on the southern Oshima Peninsula, Hokkaido

ledger.note: 1459: the Twelve Garrisons of Dōnan on the southern Oshima Peninsula are held by the Wajin again. 'In May 1457' the Ainu under Koshamain took 10 of the Twelve Garrisons; 'In 1458, Takeda Nobuhiro ... led a counteroffensive' and killed Koshamain. The page does not say the shogunate held the land; Cliopatria's Ashikaga shape grows by about 1,700 km2 in 1459.

region.text: Kyoto and Yamashiro Province, where the Ōnin War was fought

ledger.note: 1467: the Ōnin War breaks out in Kyoto. 'Then in May 1467, a Yamana mansion was attacked' (the fighting began in March when a Hosokawa mansion was burned); the page puts the most intense fighting in Kyoto and Yamashiro Province.

region.text: everything outside the Kyoto remnant: the provinces of the shugo and the daimyo

ledger.note: 1468: outside Kyoto the shogunate no longer rules. Page: during the Ōnin War (1467-1477) the shogunate 'became reduced to little more than a local political force in Kyoto'; Sengoku page: the war undermined 'the authority of the Ashikaga shoguns, greatly reducing their control over the various regions'. Cliopatria drops the shape from 322,236 to 979 km2 in 1468 and starts the Warring States Japan row. [Reviewer 2026-10-18: confidence 2 to 1; neither the Ashikaga shogunate nor the Ōnin War page gives 1468, the year is Cliopatria's.]

region.text: Kyoto and Yamashiro Province, where the Ōnin War was fought

ledger.note: 1477: the Ōnin War ends. Ōuchi Masahiro 'left the area on 17 December 1477'; 'By 1477, ten years after the fighting had begun, Kyoto was nothing more than a place for mobs to loot.'

region.text: the Kyoto holding to which the shogunate had shrunk

ledger.note: 1573: Oda Nobunaga drives Ashikaga Yoshiaki out of Kyoto and the shogunate ends. Infobox 'Ashikaga shogunate abolished: 2 September 1573'; 'The Ashikaga shogunate was finally destroyed in 1573 when Nobunaga drove Yoshiaki out of Kyoto.' Nobunaga had entered Kyoto with Yoshiaki on 18 October 1568 (infobox).

wars.name: Nanboku-chō wars (Northern and Southern Courts)

zones.text: Kyushu, the last bastion of Southern Court resistance

wars.outcome: Ashikaga victory: Kyushu resistance collapsed in 1381 and the last domain submitted in 1385; on 19 November 1392 Go-Kameyama yielded the Imperial Regalia to the Northern Court.
wars.note: Fronts the ledger does not draw: Kitabatake Chikafusa besieged in Hitachi 1338-1343 and the 1352 offensive on Takauji at Kamakura (Kantō). The Southern Court's later bases (Anau, Kongōji) are not on the page.

wars.name: Kannō disturbance
wars.outcome: Tadayoshi rebelled in 1350 and joined the Southern Court; he beat Takauji in 1351 and died suddenly in March 1352 after a second reconciliation. No border change recorded.
wars.note: A split inside the Ashikaga house, listed so the reviewer can see it was considered.

wars.name: Koshamain's revolt
belligerents: Wajin of Hanazawa (Kakizaki Sueshige, Takeda Nobuhiro)

zones.text: the Twelve Garrisons of Dōnan, southern Oshima Peninsula

wars.outcome: Wajin victory: the Ainu took 10 of the 12 garrisons in May 1457; Takeda Nobuhiro's counteroffensive in 1458 killed Koshamain and his son at Nanaehama.
wars.note: The shogunate is not a named belligerent on the page. No contest events in the ledger: the Ainu held no state (counterpart 'nobody').

wars.name: Ōnin War

zones.text: Kyoto and Yamashiro Province, where the Ōnin War was fought

wars.outcome: Ten years of fighting in Kyoto and Yamashiro that left the shogunate 'reduced to little more than a local political force in Kyoto' and began the Sengoku period; the Western Army's last major lord, Ōuchi Masahiro, left on 17 December 1477.
wars.note: The page ties the war to Yoshimasa having no heir in 1464 and a son born in 1465 (Yoshimi went to the Western side in 1468; Yoshihisa was named heir in 1469) and to the Hatakeyama clan splitting in two. The ledger draws the Kyoto zone as contested with the emerging daimyo states.

wars.name: Oda Nobunaga's entry into Kyoto and expulsion of Yoshiaki
wars.outcome: Nobunaga marched on Kyoto in 1568 'to support the 15th shogun, Ashikaga Yoshiaki' and 'expelled Ashikaga Yoshiaki from Kyoto in 1573, thus destroying the Ashikaga shogunate'.
wars.note: No border change before 1573; the Kyoto holding passes to Nobunaga's realm at the dissolve.

certainty.note: Feudal shugo and daimyo domains with no surveyed frontiers: the national outline to 1467 is the claimed realm, the Kyushu and Yoshino fronts with the Southern Court are approximate, and the post-1468 Kyoto remnant is drawn from Cliopatria's approximate outline. No treaty line exists for any frontier.

notes:
Written by Phase B agent jk-01-b on 2026-10-18 from five pages (the budget), plus the Kenmu Restoration page, which was opened for the neighbouring dossier and is cited for the 1336 handover.

Cliopatria rows: the 1344-1458 and 1459-1467 shapes are the national outline and are kept; 1468 onward is the Kyoto remnant (Warring States Japan holds the rest). The row begins 1344 although the shogunate dates from 11 August 1336, and ends 1571 although it lasted to 2 September 1573; two new keyframes (1336-1343, 1572-1573) fill the ends. The infobox gives no area, so no area comparison was possible.

Not settled for lack of pages: (1) the Kantō (Kamakura-fu / Kantō kubō, the Kōga kubō after 1455, the Kyōtoku incident) and the Kyushu Tandai are not on the pages opened; the national outline to 1458 overstates direct rule. (2) Whether the Wajin of the Twelve Garrisons of Dōnan (1459 shape) counted as shogunate land. (3) The 1540 and 1564 boundary trims of Cliopatria's Kyoto shape: no page dates them and both resolve to the same grid cells as the neighbouring shapes, so no events were written. (4) The Kannō disturbance, Hitachi siege and 1352 Kantō offensive are listed in wars but not drawn as contests. (5) Ming and Ryukyu relations (Yoshimitsu's tributary status, the 'King of Japan' title) are not on the pages and are not recorded.

Counterparts needing dossiers: southern-court (the Southern Court at Yoshino, 1337-1392; it is the counterpart of the Kyushu and Yoshino contests and of the Kenmu successor handover). warring-states-japan exists (group jk-01); its dossier should carry the matching gain in 1468 and loss in 1573.

Gazetteer: {"place": "Yoshino"} is not in places.jsonl (Yoshino mountains, Nara Prefecture, about 34.37 N 135.86 E); the gazetteer agent should add it.

Ledger ordering: the 1336 Kyushu contest has no month and therefore sorts before the 11 August found event; the page gives only the year for the retreat to Kyushu.
